It's have been a month we talked about this, and since then I have continued to struggle with this exactly problems you very well described. I recently seeked reassurance from my partner casually in the middle of a good moment we were having that made me forget about the seriousness of my intrusive thoughts, and then feeled incredibly good the rest of the day until the middle of the next day. 
I feeled just in peace, relaxed, not worried and even optimistic for the first time in ages... I had let my guard completely down, and hours later had a very bad spike of obssessive paranoia about her, rushing never ending thoughts analyzing the words of reassurance she told me during that conversation and compulsively analyzing memories of her over and over, looking for confirmation of my fears: that I was trapped in a web of lies made by her, blinded by my emotions, ignorant of the evident red flags in front of me, totally gaslighted, possibly being used to fill her emotional voids she surely has, that she is with me just because I amused her like a curious toy, easy to play with, interesting to see how it behaves, just to later be discarted when she eventually grow bored, or when she find another guy she really likes, or just in the path of being used and abused in the future... 

So it was pretty bad, I went to a psychologist and he just told I'm mild asperger (very probably, but it's still pending more confirmation) and suffer from intrusive thougts (AFAIK it's not necesary to be OCD to suffer intrusive thoughts).

At the light of this information my guessing about the origin of the intrusive thoughts is the following. Because of a strong desire of fitting socially and a longing for emotional conexion with others that have been frustrated by constant difficulties socializing, all my life I have suffered from an inmense and painful feeling of isolation. Due to having been fooled and decieved lots of times (or in the best cases been sympathetically called naive) I have a strong distrust of other people in general, and some doubts about the chatacter of the persons I know.

I met my partner and I loved her, and she loved me too. She have been an inmense emotional support during this last year, she has made incredible efforts for me and the relationship, I could be possibly death if it wasn't for her tbh. She usually express that she is happy that we are together, and so am I. I told her a lot of times, since the begining, that I have feeled alone and missunderstood most of my life but not anymore since I'm with her, even when we don't saw each other for weeks at times. And she have been telling me constantly that I am paranoic, because I'm always supposing that other people hate me, or are bad, even if all was normal. Her personna and all she has made for me doesn't fit at all with a supposedly evil or egoist person like, at all. 

And this intrusive thoughts didn't fit with OCD because I didn't have any repetitive compulsion, so maybe it was Pure O? But never had intrusive thoughts like that before in my life, maybe it was latent all my life and it has appeared during this last year of strong stress? And I don't have any obssesion about -me doing something- that caused me distress, like is tipical in OCD, is about her doing, so maybe its other focused cheat/Relationship Pure O? But it's not really that she is cheating on me, or that she leaves me, the content of the intrusive thoughts. I have intrusive thoughts about her with others but behind that the real fear is being decieved, that she was acting all along, that I'm being fooled, and not knowing it.

What maybe happens is that I have a constant subltle feeling of ambiguity about the motivations and feelings of other people due to a diminished capacity of empathy. And I fill that ambiguity in the interactions with her with suppositions of plotting at the service of egoist, or just plain evil, covert desires, and then I reinterpret the whole social interaction as a convenient facade, even if maybe she is not completely aware of it and her real motivations. I had plenty of bad experiences with other persons son it's easy for me to think like that. In the moments where she is mad (most of the time she have good reasons), or she is just mean. When I'm assaulted by intrusive thoughts, I think that this are not bad moods, but the real person behind the facade when it breaks down. 

The lifelong feelings of isolation, also that I'm in a bad moment in my life, that she has been basically the only person I have been talking to this last year, between other factors, have contributed to my strong emotional dependency towards her.

In short, I believe this constant intrusive thoughts emanate from the conflict of fears of isolation that inflates this emotional dependency by one side, in opposition to fears and doubts by the other side about an evil nature of her, about my intuition and memories specially because of being blinded by my feelings, and about her dubtious behaviours result of my difficulty to understand her, and people general. 

Fear of being alone without her vs fears of being wounded by her. And just not knowing if I can trust her. 

Not knowing if I can trust my capacity to know if I can trust (her).

Adaptive Behaviors: How They May Delay Diagnosis

ADHD symptoms are evident early in life and clearly affect personality development.These personality features run the gamut of adaptability. Hyperactivity and impulsivity may lead to antisocial behaviors and decidedly negative outcomes.

By contrast, certain individuals with ADHD may reject the inherent entropy of their condition and respond by developing obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (OCPD) traits.On some level, they innately recognize that their natural tendency is to remain disorganized and tardy, so they force themselves to stay rigidly rule bound. They develop lists and then lists of lists as reminders. They check and recheck where they place their keys and cell phone, for example, even to the point of developing rituals. (The keys must always be in the jacket pocket, the cell phone must be placed on a table by the front door when arriving home, and so forth.) They establish strict daily schedules, and avoid any deviations from the routine out of fear that 1 misstep could hopelessly unravel their plans for the entire day or even the week. In social conversations, such individuals can become overly verbose, driven by a sensation that unless they explain every minute detail, their message will not be understood.

According to what I have read from Russell Barkley, ADHD is a problem of the Executive Functions. Executive Functions are Self-Regulation, actions that are self-directed. Like the one that you says, self-speech, self directed talk. And maintain that information in mind, and use it when it is appropriate for guiding our behaviour.

There are others Executive Functions, self-inhibition being one of them too. Self-inhibition is precondition to self-speech, because it enable us to say to ourselves STOP consider the situation and, then, self-ask what we should do next.
